articles.title: Sri Lanka receives Rs. 330 Mn worth of cancer medicines from US charity
articles.text:
Sri Lanka has received a donation of essential cancer medicines worth Rs. 330 million from a US-based charitable organisation, while an agreement has also been signed to provide 600 specialised wheelchairs for patients with spinal cord injuries.
The donation was made by Latter-day Saint Charities (LDSC), affiliated with The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, to the Ministry of Health and Mass Media on Wednesday (14).
According to the Ministry, the donated medicines include several essential oncology drugs, such as Oxaliplatin 100mg injections, Abiraterone 250mg tablets and Methotrexate 500mg/5ml injections, intended for the treatment of cancer patients in Sri Lanka.
The medicines were officially handed over to Ministry Secretary Dr. Anil Jasinghe by LDSC Asia Area Director Lui Wing Chung Mickey and Asia Area Manager Apapohn Pinsakol Saengsin at the Ministry premises.
During the event, a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) was also signed between the Ministry and the US-based organisation for the donation of 600 specialised wheelchairs to rehabilitation hospitals and centres treating patients with spinal cord injuries.
The wheelchair donation marks the second phase of the organisation’s humanitarian assistance programme in Sri Lanka.
Under the first phase in 2023, LDSC donated 570 wheelchairs, which have since been distributed to patients through rehabilitation centres across the country.
The latest programme will also include specialised training for healthcare personnel on wheelchair prescription, use and repairs, in accordance with World Health Organization (WHO) guidelines.
Doctors, physiotherapists, occupational therapists and wheelchair workshop staff are expected to receive training under the initiative.
Meanwhile, the Ministry noted that LDSC had also donated essential cancer medicines worth approximately US$ 2 million (Rs. 660 million) to Sri Lanka over the past two years.
In recognition of the latest donation, a special Certificate of Appreciation arranged by Minister of Health Nalinda Jayatissa was presented to the organisation’s Asia Area Director by Ministry Secretary Dr. Anil Jasinghe.
articles.summary: Sri Lanka has received a donation of essential cancer medicines worth Rs. 330 million from a US-based charitable organisation, while an agreement has also been signed to provide 600 specialised wheelchairs for patients with spinal cord injuries. Meanwhile, the Ministry noted that LDSC had also donated essential cancer medicines worth approximately US$ 2 million (Rs. 660 million) to Sri Lanka over the past two years.

articles.title: New website launched for public inquiries on education reforms
articles.text:
The Government has launched a new official website to provide accurate information and address public inquiries regarding Sri Lanka’s proposed education reforms.
The Reform Information & Enquiry Service (RIES) website, https://edureformfact.moe.gov.lk , was officially launched with the participation of Prime Minister and Minister of Education, Higher Education and Vocational Education Harini Amarasuriya.
The launch took place during a programme held at Temple Trees yesterday (14), attended by heads of electronic and print media institutions to discuss the implementation of the new education reforms.
The website has been developed to communicate accurate information about the reforms and allow members of the public to submit questions regarding the proposed changes to the education system.
Addressing the gathering, Prime Minister Amarasuriya emphasised that the reforms represent a transformation of the entire education system rather than merely a revision of the school curriculum.
“This is a transformation of the entire education system that goes beyond a change in the curriculum. The future of our country is built on quality education,” she stated.
The Prime Minister noted that the first phase of the reforms commenced with Grade 1 in 2026, while plans are underway to introduce the reforms to Grade 6 in 2027.
She said teacher training, infrastructure development and digitalisation initiatives are already being implemented to ensure the education system is prepared for the changes.
Highlighting the role of the media, the Prime Minister stressed the importance of creating a national dialogue on education reforms and ensuring that accurate information reaches the public.
“We may have different political ideologies, but it is important that we do not use children’s education as a political battleground,” she said.
Meanwhile, Professor Prabhath Jayasinghe, Co-Chairperson of the Subcommittee on Public Awareness of Education Reforms, explained that the proposed changes aim to move away from teacher-centred, memorisation-based education towards student-centred learning connected to real-world experiences.
He said the reforms would also introduce continuous assessment methods to evaluate students’ analytical, creative and problem-solving abilities, rather than relying primarily on final examinations.
The programme concluded with a discussion among media representatives, senior journalists and education experts on the proposed changes to Sri Lanka’s education system.
articles.summary: The Government has launched a new official website to provide accurate information and address public inquiries regarding Sri Lanka’s proposed education reforms. The Reform Information & Enquiry Service (RIES) website, https://edureformfact.moe.gov.lk , was officially launched with the participation of Prime Minister and Minister of Education, Higher Education and Vocational Education Harini Amarasuriya.

articles.title: Dehiwala Zoo Zebra recovering well after successful emergency surgery
articles.text:
A zebra at the Dehiwala National Zoological Gardens is recovering well and has resumed eating normally following a successful emergency surgery to remove an obstruction from its digestive tract.
The Department of National Zoological Gardens, providing an update on the animal’s condition, confirmed that the zebra is making a rapid recovery under veterinary care.
According to the Department, the zebra had been showing signs of illness since September 29, prompting veterinary officers to conduct laboratory tests and a scan.
The examinations revealed an obstruction in the animal’s digestive tract, requiring urgent surgical intervention.
Accordingly, a special emergency surgery was performed on October 9, with the participation of veterinary officers and staff of the Department of National Zoological Gardens.
The procedure was conducted under the guidance and participation of Dr. Dammika Perera, Senior Lecturer at the Faculty of Veterinary Medicine of the University of Peradeniya, who specialises in equine species.
The surgery continued for several hours until the early hours of the following morning, during which veterinary surgeons successfully removed a mass of undigested food that had caused the obstruction.
Following the procedure, the zebra was kept under close veterinary supervision for several days.
The Department has now confirmed that the animal is recovering well and has resumed its usual feeding habits.
The Department of National Zoological Gardens also expressed appreciation to Dr. Dammika Perera, veterinary surgeon Dr. Hasitha Rupathunga, the Dehiwala Zoo Veterinary Hospital staff and animal care teams for their contributions to the successful surgery and the zebra’s recovery.

articles.summary: A zebra at the Dehiwala National Zoological Gardens is recovering well and has resumed eating normally following a successful emergency surgery to remove an obstruction from its digestive tract.

articles.title: Monk who linked assault to NPP now says he assumed victim was protest supporter
articles.text:
Ven. Thiththagalle Anandasiri Thera has responded to allegations by Sri Lanka Police that he spread false information about an assault during a protest march demanding the release of imprisoned Buddhist monk Ven. Galagoda Aththe Gnanasara Thera, acknowledging that he had initially assumed the injured man was a supporter of the march.
In his initial video, the monk alleged that individuals linked to the ruling National People’s Power (NPP) were responsible for attacking a man who had assisted the protest march from Kandy to Colombo.
However, responding to a police statement rejecting those claims, the monk said he had believed the injured man was someone supporting the march because the assault occurred in front of the protesters.
He did not repeat his earlier allegation directly linking the attackers to the NPP in his latest explanation, instead focusing on the police response to the incident.
The monk maintained that the assault had occurred in the presence of police officers deployed along the protest route and questioned why they had allegedly failed to intervene.
According to Ven. Anandasiri Thera, the victim was bleeding following the attack, and he helped clean the man’s wounds before arranging for him to be taken to hospital by ambulance.
He also claimed that those accompanying the march had recorded the registration number of the motorcycle involved and provided the information to police.
The monk questioned why police had focused on accusing him of spreading misinformation rather than examining the alleged failure of officers to act when the assault occurred.
He further suggested that police had taken action only after his video attracted public attention.
His response follows a statement issued by Sri Lanka Police on Oct. 15, rejecting claims that a supporter of the march had been attacked.
Police said investigations revealed that the incident occurred on Oct. 14 near the Veediyawatta Devalaya in the Weeragula police area following a traffic-related dispute between a man travelling in a lorry and a motorcyclist.
According to police, an argument arising from traffic congestion escalated into a confrontation during which the lorry occupant was struck with a helmet.
Police said the injured man had confirmed in a statement that he was travelling for personal reasons and had no connection to the protest march.
The injured man was admitted to Wathupitiwala Hospital, while the motorcyclist involved in the dispute was also admitted to Gampaha Hospital for treatment.
Police accused Ven. Anandasiri Thera of misleading the public by presenting the injured man as a supporter of the march who had been deliberately attacked.
The monk, however, rejected suggestions that he had deliberately spread false information, maintaining that he had intervened to help an injured person and publicised the incident to draw attention to the assault.
He also criticised the government’s handling of the protest and reiterated that the march would continue towards Colombo despite heavy rain.
Police said the matter would be reported to court and warned that legal action could be taken against those spreading false or unverified information capable of causing public unrest.
Further investigations are underway.
articles.summary: Ven. Thiththagalle Anandasiri Thera has responded to allegations by Sri Lanka Police that he spread false information about an assault during a protest march demanding the release of imprisoned Buddhist monk Ven. Galagoda Aththe Gnanasara Thera, acknowledging that he had initially assumed the injured man was a supporter of the march.

articles.title: SC grants leave to appeal in former Deputy Minister’s Rs. 50,000 bribery case
articles.text:
The Supreme Court has granted special leave to appeal in a bribery case involving former Deputy Minister Shantha Premaratne, who was sentenced to four years of rigorous imprisonment for soliciting and accepting a Rs. 50,000 bribe in exchange for promising employment.
Premaratne, a former United People’s Freedom Alliance (UPFA) politician and Sri Lanka Freedom Party (SLFP) organiser in the Ampara District, was convicted by the High Court in 2017.
According to the Bribery Commission, Premaratne had solicited and accepted Rs. 50,000 from a party supporter after promising to secure employment for her son-in-law at the Ceylon Electricity Board (CEB).
The Court of Appeal upheld his conviction on Nov. 5, 2024, prompting Premaratne to challenge the ruling before the Supreme Court.
A three-judge bench comprising Justices Achala Wengappuli, Arjuna Obeyesekere and Gihan Kulatunga granted special leave to appeal on the question of whether the charge in the indictment had been proved during the trial.
Premaratne has maintained that the money was received as a donation towards the construction of a party headquarters and not as a bribe in exchange for employment.
He also claimed that political rivals had instigated complaints against him after he lost a party selection contest in June 2008.
The Supreme Court fixed the appeal for argument on March 29, 2027.
Attorneys Hafeel Farisz, Prashan Wickramaratne and Sanjeewa Kodithuwakku appeared for Premaratne, while Additional Director General Ruvini Wickramasinghe represented the Bribery Commission.
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has granted special leave to appeal in a bribery case involving former Deputy Minister Shantha Premaratne, who was sentenced to four years of rigorous imprisonment for soliciting and accepting a Rs. 50,000 bribe in exchange for promising employment.

articles.title: Over 14,300 visas issued to foreigners through Port City recommendations: Parliament raises monitoring concerns
articles.text:
Sri Lanka’s Parliamentary Committee on Public Finance has raised concerns over the monitoring of foreign nationals after it was revealed that approximately 14,300 visas had been issued on the recommendation of the Colombo Port City Economic Commission.
The matter was discussed during a committee meeting held on Oct. 8 under the chairmanship of MP Dr. Harsha de Silva, according to a parliamentary statement issued on Oct. 15.
Committee members examined the practical feasibility of monitoring the activities of foreign nationals who had obtained visas through recommendations made by the Port City Commission.
The discussions focused on the issuance of visa recommendations for foreign workers and the mechanisms available to monitor their activities within the country.
The committee also emphasized the importance of strengthening regulatory measures to prevent illegal activities within Colombo Port City and safeguard Sri Lanka’s international reputation.
Meanwhile, members questioned the mechanisms used to identify the beneficial owners of companies investing in Port City, ensure transparency in foreign investments and prevent money laundering and terrorist financing.
The committee also reviewed the progress of investment projects within Colombo Port City.
Officials revealed that nine land plots valued at approximately US$1.12 billion had already been leased, while plans were underway to lease another six plots worth US$1 billion.
The Commission also informed the committee that four government-owned land plots were being prepared for the market.
According to officials, the land had been leased for 99 years at an average value of US$3,000 per square metre.
The committee further examined whether businesses approved to operate within Port City had commenced operations and whether the expected foreign investments and employment opportunities had materialized.
Concerns were also raised regarding the protection of deposits paid by investors purchasing condominium units, particularly the use of escrow accounts to ensure that funds were used exclusively for the relevant development projects.
The discussions were attended by Deputy Ministers Chathuranga Abeysinghe and Nishantha Jayawera, along with several government and opposition MPs.
articles.summary: Sri Lanka’s Parliamentary Committee on Public Finance has raised concerns over the monitoring of foreign nationals after it was revealed that approximately 14,300 visas had been issued on the recommendation of the Colombo Port City Economic Commission. Committee members examined the practical feasibility of monitoring the activities of foreign nationals who had obtained visas through recommendations made by the Port City Commission.

articles.title: TISL warns new anti-terrorism Bill could restrict public protests and freedom of expression
tags: Protection of the State from Terrorism
articles.text:
Transparency International Sri Lanka (TISL) has raised serious concerns over the proposed Protection of the State from Terrorism Bill, warning that several provisions could undermine fundamental rights, judicial independence and democratic freedoms.
In a statement , TISL expressed concern over the Bill, gazetted on September 22, 2026, which seeks to replace the existing Prevention of Terrorism Act (PTA).
The organisation highlighted concerns regarding the Bill’s broad definition of terrorism, expanded executive powers, administrative detention provisions and restrictions on fundamental freedoms.
TISL warned that the proposed definition of terrorism covers a wide range of activities, including damage to property, the environment, cultural property and electronic systems, potentially bringing offences that should be addressed under ordinary criminal law within the scope of terrorism legislation.
It further cautioned that the broad definitions could result in disproportionate restrictions on freedom of expression, association and legitimate civic activities.
The organisation also raised concerns over provisions granting the armed forces and Coast Guard extensive powers of arrest, search, seizure and questioning, warning that insufficient safeguards could create accountability gaps and increase the risk of arbitrary action.
Regarding detention provisions, TISL noted that the Bill allows the Secretary to the Ministry of Defence to issue detention orders for an initial period of two months, while limiting the Magistrate’s authority to independently assess the necessity of detention.
The organisation warned that these provisions could concentrate excessive powers within the executive while weakening judicial oversight.
TISL also expressed concern over provisions allowing the President to proscribe organisations, noting that the absence of specified time limits and adequate safeguards could lead to arbitrary restrictions on freedom of association and civic activities.
While acknowledging the State’s responsibility to address legitimate national security concerns, TISL stressed that counter-terrorism legislation must not undermine fundamental rights, due process or judicial independence.
TISL urged the Government to withdraw the proposed Protection of the State from Terrorism Bill 2026 and repeal the existing Prevention of Terrorism Act without further delay.
The organisation further called for any replacement legislation to establish clear limits on executive authority, effective accountability mechanisms and adequate safeguards against arbitrary detention and the misuse of counter-terrorism powers.
articles.summary: Transparency International Sri Lanka (TISL) has raised serious concerns over the proposed Protection of the State from Terrorism Bill, warning that several provisions could undermine fundamental rights, judicial independence and democratic freedoms. In a statement , TISL expressed concern over the Bill, gazetted on September 22, 2026, which seeks to replace the existing Prevention of Terrorism Act (PTA).

articles.title: LOLC rejects allegations over People’s Bank loan facility, warns of legal action
articles.text:
LOLC Holdings PLC has strongly rejected allegations circulating on social media concerning a banking facility involving People’s Bank, describing the claims as misleading and factually inaccurate.
In a clarification submitted to the Colombo Stock Exchange (CSE) on Oct. 14, LOLC said the local-currency borrowing was fully secured against a US dollar deposit maintained with People’s Bank itself.
The company stressed that People’s Bank holds the full collateral supporting the facility, rejecting suggestions that the bank was exposed to unsecured lending or that public deposits were at risk.
LOLC explained that, as part of its global treasury operations, its group companies maintain US dollar deposits with international and local banks, including People’s Bank.
These deposits are used as security to obtain local-currency funding without converting the underlying dollar assets into Sri Lankan rupees.
The company said such arrangements are conventional treasury and foreign-exchange risk management practices adopted by multinational businesses operating across different countries.
LOLC, which operates in 27 countries, also dismissed claims suggesting that the deposit was located overseas or that People’s Bank would have difficulty recovering the funds.
It further rejected allegations that the transaction involved questionable banking practices, foreign-exchange speculation or improper use of public funds.
Meanwhile, LOLC warned that it was bringing publications containing materially misleading information to the attention of relevant regulatory and other authorities.
The company said it reserved the right to pursue legal action against individuals and organizations responsible for originating, publishing or knowingly republishing false or misleading information, where applicable legal requirements are met.
LOLC reiterated its commitment to transparent and responsible operations, stating that it would take necessary steps to protect the interests of the group and its stakeholders.
articles.summary: LOLC Holdings PLC has strongly rejected allegations circulating on social media concerning a banking facility involving People’s Bank, describing the claims as misleading and factually inaccurate. In a clarification submitted to the Colombo Stock Exchange (CSE) on Oct. 14, LOLC said the local-currency borrowing was fully secured against a US dollar deposit maintained with People’s Bank itself.

articles.title: Petrol-only cars fall below 50% of global new vehicle sales for first time in history
articles.text:
Petrol-only vehicles have accounted for less than half of global new vehicle sales for the first time on record, marking a significant shift in the global automotive industry as hybrid and electric vehicles continue to gain popularity.
According to automotive industry data reported by Japan’s Nikkei newspaper, petrol-only vehicles accounted for approximately 49% of global new vehicle sales during the first half of 2026, down from 52% during the same period in 2025.
The figures represent a sharp decline from 2021, when petrol-only vehicles accounted for approximately 73% of global new vehicle sales.
During the January-June 2026 period, around 20.25 million petrol-only vehicles were sold worldwide, representing a year-on-year decline of approximately 10%.
The shift reflects growing consumer demand for hybrid, plug-in hybrid and fully electric vehicles, supported by advances in battery technology, expanding charging infrastructure and increasing competition among automakers.
However, the decline in petrol-only vehicles does not mean that electric vehicles now dominate the global market.
A significant portion of the remaining market consists of hybrid vehicles, which continue to use petrol engines alongside electric motors.
The development marks an important milestone in the global automotive industry’s transition toward electrification, as traditional petrol-only vehicles lose their long-standing majority share of new vehicle sales.
articles.summary: Petrol-only vehicles have accounted for less than half of global new vehicle sales for the first time on record, marking a significant shift in the global automotive industry as hybrid and electric vehicles continue to gain popularity.

articles.title: Sri Lanka named Leading Wellness Destination at South Asian Travel Awards 2026
articles.text:
Sri Lanka has won the Visitors’ Choice Award for Leading Wellness Destination at the 10th South Asian Travel Awards (SATA) 2026, held in Malé, Maldives, on October 8.
Sri Lanka’s High Commissioner to the Maldives, M. Rizvi Hassen, received the award at the ceremony, which brought together tourism and hospitality industry representatives from across South Asia.
According to the Sri Lankan High Commission in the Maldives, the recognition highlights the country’s rich heritage of Ayurveda and traditional healing practices, along with its diverse natural landscapes and wellness tourism experiences that continue to attract international visitors.
The South Asian Travel Awards recognise excellence in the tourism and hospitality sectors across six countries: Sri Lanka, India, Maldives, Nepal, Bhutan and Bangladesh.
The awards cover several categories, including hotels, resorts, travel agencies, tour operators, airlines and other tourism-related organisations.
This year’s awards attracted more than two million online votes, alongside evaluations conducted by a multinational panel of judges across seven cities.
The 2026 ceremony was held at Barceló Nasandhura Malé in the Maldives, marking the 10th edition of the regional awards programme.
Established in 2016, SATA has become a regional platform recognising achievements and excellence in South Asia’s travel, tourism and hospitality industries.

articles.title: IMF ready to support Sri Lanka beyond current programme : Senior official
articles.text:
The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has reaffirmed its commitment to supporting Sri Lanka, emphasizing that it will remain a trusted partner as the country continues its economic recovery and approaches the completion of its current IMF programme.
IMF Deputy Division Chief in the Asia and Pacific Department, Sonali Jain-Chandra, said the Fund stands ready to support Sri Lanka through future financing arrangements, policy advice or capacity development, depending on the government’s requirements.
“The Fund will remain a very committed partner to Sri Lanka,” she stated, emphasizing that the nature of future engagement would be determined through discussions with the Sri Lankan authorities.
Highlighting the progress achieved under the current IMF programme, Jain-Chandra noted significant improvements in macroeconomic stability, government revenue, debt restructuring and economic growth.
“The macroeconomic situation is much improved. The revenue ratio has doubled. The debt restructuring is largely complete. Growth has been positive for 11 consecutive quarters,” she said.
She also highlighted improvements in governance and other structural reforms, describing the programme’s overall performance as strong.
However, Jain-Chandra stressed that important work remains under the existing programme, which is scheduled to expire in March.
She noted that a staff-level agreement on the seventh review had been reached in early October and that it was expected to be considered by the IMF Executive Board in the coming weeks.
Another review mission is also scheduled to take place before the programme expires.
The IMF official emphasized the importance of maintaining macroeconomic stability and consolidating the reform gains achieved so far.
Addressing the possibility of future IMF assistance, Jain-Chandra explained that requesting another programme would be a decision for the Sri Lankan authorities.
“There are many ways in which the Fund can support Sri Lanka, whether it’s a new financing arrangement, whether it’s granular policy advice in the context of surveillance or capacity development,” she said.
She reiterated that the IMF remains prepared to continue its engagement with Sri Lanka in a manner that supports the country’s economic priorities.
IMF Deputy Division Chief in the Asia and Pacific Department, Sonali Jain-Chandra, stated this while clarifying details regarding Sri Lanka’s economic progress during a press conference held this morning (15), which took place alongside the annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank Group in Bangkok, Thailand.
articles.summary: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has reaffirmed its commitment to supporting Sri Lanka, emphasizing that it will remain a trusted partner as the country continues its economic recovery and approaches the completion of its current IMF programme.

articles.title: Arugam Bay named Asia’s best beach for 2026, four Sri Lankan beaches in top 20
articles.text:
Sri Lanka’s Arugam Bay has been ranked Asia’s best beach for 2026 in the Condé Nast Traveller Readers’ Choice Awards, with four Sri Lankan beaches securing places among the region’s top 20.
Arugam Bay, a popular surfing destination on Sri Lanka’s eastern coast, secured first place, ahead of Railay Beach in Thailand and Coral Beach in Malaysia.
Three other Sri Lankan destinations also featured in the rankings, with Bentota Beach placed ninth, Tangalle Beach 14th and Negombo Beach 19th.
The recognition highlights Sri Lanka’s appeal as a beach tourism destination, with the four locations representing different coastal regions of the island.
The top five beaches in Asia were Arugam Bay in Sri Lanka, Railay Beach in Thailand, Coral Beach in Malaysia, Boracay in the Philippines and Nusa Dua Beach in Indonesia.
The Readers’ Choice Awards are based on ratings submitted by Condé Nast Traveller readers, reflecting travellers’ experiences and preferences.
Arugam Bay received a score of 98.84, the highest in the Asian rankings, followed by Railay Beach with 94.44 and Coral Beach with 93.33.
Bentota received a score of 88.33, Tangalle 83.33 and Negombo 78.92.
The 2026 awards, published on Oct. 6, marked the 29th edition of the annual survey, with results based on votes from the magazine’s UK readership.
articles.summary: Sri Lanka’s Arugam Bay has been ranked Asia’s best beach for 2026 in the Condé Nast Traveller Readers’ Choice Awards, with four Sri Lankan beaches securing places among the region’s top 20. The top five beaches in Asia were Arugam Bay in Sri Lanka, Railay Beach in Thailand, Coral Beach in Malaysia, Boracay in the Philippines and Nusa Dua Beach in Indonesia.

articles.title: From Bangkok with beauty products: Rs. 51 million secret uncovered at BIA
articles.text:
Three Thai nationals have been arrested at the Bandaranaike International Airport (BIA) in Katunayake for allegedly attempting to smuggle hashish worth approximately Rs. 51 million into Sri Lanka.
The suspects were arrested by officers of the Police Narcotics Bureau (PNB) early today (15), while attempting to leave the airport with the narcotics.
The arrested suspects, aged 22, 22 and 33, are reportedly employed as drivers in Thailand.
According to reports, the three suspects arrived at Katunayake Airport from Bangkok, Thailand, aboard Thai Airways flight TG-307 at approximately 12.30 a.m. today.
During an inspection of their three pieces of luggage, officers discovered 5.96 kilograms of hashish, carefully concealed inside cosmetic product containers.
The three suspects, along with the seized narcotics, are scheduled to be produced before the Negombo Magistrate’s Court today (15).
The Police Narcotics Bureau at Katunayake Airport is conducting further investigations.

articles.title: Sri Lankan Deputy Minister and MP participate in Commonwealth Parliamentary Residency
articles.text:
Sri Lankan Deputy Minister Kaushalya Ariyaratne and MP Kavinda Jayawardena are participating in the Commonwealth Parliamentary Association’s (CPA) Advanced Parliamentary Development Residency Programme, being held in St Peter Port, Guernsey, from October 12 to 16, 2026.
The five-day programme, organised by the CPA Parliamentary Academy with the support of Guernsey’s parliament, the States of Deliberation, brings together around 30 parliamentarians from across the Commonwealth.
Deputy Minister Kaushalya Ariyaratne and Gampaha District Samagi Jana Balawegaya (SJB) MP Kavinda Jayawardena, are attending the programme on behalf of Sri Lanka.
Participants include representatives from Kenya, Namibia, Malta, Pakistan, Saint Lucia, Canada, Australia and Guernsey.
The programme focuses on strengthening parliamentary practices, including legislative scrutiny, committee work, communication and the evolving role of parliamentarians in the 21st century.
As part of the programme, participants engaged in a simulated parliamentary debate on the Reform (Guernsey) (Amendment) Law, 2025, which addresses the procedure for filling vacant seats in Guernsey’s parliament.
The residency also includes mentoring sessions, committee simulations and engagement with Guernsey’s parliamentary institutions.
The initiative aims to enhance parliamentary skills, encourage the exchange of experiences and strengthen cooperation among parliamentarians across the Commonwealth.
articles.summary: Sri Lankan Deputy Minister Kaushalya Ariyaratne and MP Kavinda Jayawardena are participating in the Commonwealth Parliamentary Association’s (CPA) Advanced Parliamentary Development Residency Programme, being held in St Peter Port, Guernsey, from October 12 to 16, 2026. The five-day programme, organised by the CPA Parliamentary Academy with the support of Guernsey’s parliament, the States of Deliberation, brings together around 30 parliamentarians from across the Commonwealth.

articles.title: Severe lightning and strong winds expected in several parts of Sri Lanka
articles.text:
The Department of Meteorology has issued a severe lightning advisory for several parts of Sri Lanka, with red alerts issued for 18 districts and amber alerts for seven districts.
According to the department, the advisory was issued at 11.00 a.m. today (15) and will remain valid until 1.00 a.m. tomorrow (16).
Thundershowers accompanied by severe lightning are likely at several places in the North-Central, Eastern, Central, Sabaragamuwa and Uva provinces, as well as in the Kilinochchi, Mullaitivu, Vavuniya, Gampaha, Colombo and Kurunegala districts.
The Met Department also warned that temporary localized strong winds may occur during thunderstorms.
The public has been urged to take adequate precautions to minimize damage and risks associated with lightning activity and strong winds.
The Department advised residents in the affected areas to remain vigilant during the advisory period.

articles.title: New militant group in Bangladesh, government alert
articles.text:
A new militant group has emerged in Bangladesh under the name “Ittihadul Ummah.” Intelligence agencies are currently investigating whether they have links to foreign militant organizations. This information came to light following the interrogation of individuals recently detained from the Tejgaon College mosque. Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed confirmed the news regarding “Ittihadul Ummah.”
The Home Minister stated, “Through forensic analysis of the mobile phones of the individuals taken into custody in Tejgaon and their subsequent interrogation, we obtained information about plans to form an organization named ‘Ittihadul Ummah.’ They are accused of organizing extremist activities aimed at establishing a Caliphate.” However, the Bangladesh Government has issued an alert, emphasizing a strict crackdown on all forms of militant activity.
The Home Minister added, “We have a zero-tolerance policy against such extremist activities.”
Recently, police detained 23 individuals from a mosque at Tejgaon College in the capital, Dhaka, on suspicion of involvement with banned militant organizations. Acting on a secret tip-off, police apprehended them while they were holding a clandestine meeting after Friday prayers on September 18. A senior officer from the Tejgaon Division of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) briefed journalists about the successful operation. This arrest of militants in Tejgaon has once again brought militant activity in Bangladesh into focus. Notably, the United Nations had previously warned South Asian nations regarding various militant networks, including Al-Qaeda.
According to police sources, the detainees were apprehended during their secret meeting based on intelligence inputs. Officials from the Anti-Terrorism Unit (ATU) and the Counter Terrorism and Transnational Crime (CTTC) unit took them into CTTC custody for verification and questioning. Interrogations are bringing to light various details about their militant activities. Under the patronage of fundamentalists, militant activity has been on the rise in Bangladesh. Furthermore, a deep conspiracy is underway to destabilize the country by unseating the elected government of Bangladesh, leveraging religious sentiments and foreign backing from behind the scenes.
The day after the arrests in Tejgaon, on Saturday, September 19, three buses were set on fire in Mirpur and Madhya Badda. A pickup van was also torched in South Keraniganj. Additionally, crude bomb explosions occurred in various locations across the capital, with more reported on Sunday in several areas. Overall, attempts are being made to create an atmosphere of panic. Intelligence officials believe defeated political forces are fueling these acts to destabilize Bangladesh. However, due to strict police vigilance, the situation currently remains under control.
Religious fundamentalism and militant activities have surged in Bangladesh since the era of the interim government. Following the formation of the new government under Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, a zero-tolerance policy against militancy was adopted. After taking office, Zahed Ur Rahman, the Information Adviser to the Prime Minister, stated, “Militants exist in the country, and the government will work to bring militant activities down to zero.” The government is working toward that goal; however, opposition factions continue to patronize militants to put the government in a tight spot. Their game of destabilizing the nation constantly compromises public safety.
Since the July uprising, numerous militants have been roaming free. Three internationally listed hardline militant leaders who escaped from prison are still at large. Among the escaped prisoners, 9 were accused in multiple terrorism cases, and several were alleged to have ties with international terror organizations. So far, 6 of them have been rearrested, but the remaining three remain untraced, Inspector General of Prisons (IG Prisons) Brigadier General Syed Motaher Hossain told reporters.
Although prison authorities lack exact figures, it is known that at least 27 militants escaped from Narsingdi Jail alone. During the July ’24 mass uprising, at least 690 prisoners escaped from various jails across the country, many of whom are still unaccounted for. According to various sources, these fugitive militants are teaming up with fundamentalists to form new terror outfits in Bangladesh, aiming to create panic by attacking minorities.
Interrogating those arrested in Tejgaon, intelligence officers learned that the militants planned to organize under the new banner “Ittihadul Ummah” to establish a Caliphate. Following recent events, concerns over radicalism are escalating once again. Law enforcement agencies, however, state that there is currently insufficient evidence to view the situation as a full-blown resurgence of extremism, though potential activities are under close surveillance. Drawing from past experiences, the general public favors immediate and strict action. In their view, to keep the nation free from extremism, militancy must be nipped in the bud.
Militancy has long thrived in Bangladesh, expanding its footprint under the guise of religion through foreign funds and assistance. According to human rights activist Nur Khan Liton, extremism is not a new phenomenon in Bangladesh; its presence has been a long-standing concern. In response to questions from journalists, he remarked, “How effectively these groups were monitored over the past two years is a critical question. We are now seeing indicators that they are attempting to reorganize.”
The web of militancy has even spread inside disciplined forces like the Bangladesh Air Force. This year, a Warrant Officer of the Bangladesh Air Force, who went missing from a base in Chattogram, was traced to a hideout of the banned militant outfit Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP). Following this incident, an internal investigation was launched into the presence of extremist networks within the armed forces. The Pakistani government recently informed Bangladeshi authorities that a Bangladesh Air Force member was fighting alongside the TTP against their military. Militant infiltration into the defense forces poses a severe threat to the country’s independence and sovereignty. Equally dangerous is the sowing of militant seeds in young minds through madrasas, which must be counteracted through even stricter vigilance. (Daily Sun)
articles.summary: A new militant group has emerged in Bangladesh under the name “Ittihadul Ummah. However, the Bangladesh Government has issued an alert, emphasizing a strict crackdown on all forms of militant activity.

articles.title: US Embassy issues financial preparedness reminder for Sri Lankan visa applicants
articles.text:
The United States Embassy in Sri Lanka has reminded nonimmigrant visa applicants to ensure they have sufficient financial resources to cover their expenses during travel to the United States, including unexpected travel disruptions and medical emergencies.
In a statement, the Embassy advised individuals planning to travel to the US to be financially prepared and provide supporting evidence during their visa interviews.
Applicants have been encouraged to present documentation demonstrating their ability to support themselves financially and showing that they are unlikely to become a public charge after entering the United States.
The Embassy emphasized that travellers should be prepared to meet their own expenses throughout their stay, including costs arising from unforeseen circumstances.
Meanwhile, the Embassy also issued a warning against submitting false documents during the visa application process.
It stressed that presenting fraudulent documents constitutes visa fraud and could result in visa disqualification and even permanent ineligibility to obtain a US visa.
The reminder is aimed at ensuring that prospective travellers understand the financial preparedness and documentation expectations associated with the US nonimmigrant visa application process.

articles.title: Sri Lanka promotes pure Ceylon Cinnamon in India’s Mumbai market
articles.text:
Sri Lanka has showcased its world-renowned Pure Ceylon Cinnamon in Mumbai, India, as part of efforts to expand export opportunities and strengthen trade ties with India’s hospitality, culinary and wellness sectors.
According to the Consulate General of Sri Lanka in Mumbai, the trade showcase titled “The Ceylon Cinnamon Story – A Sri Lankan Legacy” was held at Lisa’s Lanka in Bandra on October 7, 2026, under the Economic Diplomacy Programme of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Foreign Employment and Tourism.
The event brought together diplomats, Indian trade officials, representatives of the Indian Hotel and Restaurant Association (AHAR), chambers of commerce, industry experts, chefs and influencers to promote the heritage, quality and commercial value of Pure Ceylon Cinnamon.
Addressing the gathering, Sri Lankan Consul General Priyanga Wickramasinghe highlighted the historical significance and economic importance of Ceylon Cinnamon as one of Sri Lanka’s flagship spice exports.
The event also highlighted Ceylon Cinnamon’s recognition as the first Sri Lankan product to receive Protected Geographical Indication (PGI) status from the European Union in 2022, recognizing its geographical origin and distinctive qualities.
Meanwhile, Minister (Commercial) of the Consulate General Shirani Ariyarathne delivered a presentation on the spice’s history, cultivation, traditional craftsmanship, certification, grades and culinary applications.
The presentation also highlighted Ceylon Cinnamon’s distinctive floral-citrus flavour and significantly lower coumarin content compared to cassia cinnamon.
Visitors were introduced to various grades of Ceylon Cinnamon, including Alba, Continental, Mexican and Hamburg, alongside value-added products such as cinnamon powder, cut quills, cinnamon leaf oil and cinnamon bark oil.
The showcase also featured live cooking demonstrations and tasting sessions by Chef Lisa Sadanah, highlighting the use of Pure Ceylon Cinnamon in savoury dishes, mocktails, desserts and infusions.
The Consulate General stated that the initiative forms part of Sri Lanka’s ongoing efforts to promote its exports and expand commercial partnerships in Western India, particularly in Mumbai, a major hub for hospitality and international trade.
articles.summary: Sri Lanka has showcased its world-renowned Pure Ceylon Cinnamon in Mumbai, India, as part of efforts to expand export opportunities and strengthen trade ties with India’s hospitality, culinary and wellness sectors.

articles.title: Ceylon Tea, Kottu and Vadai take centre stage at FAO exhibition in Italy
articles.text:
Sri Lanka’s world-renowned Ceylon Tea and popular street foods, including Kottu and Parippu Vadai, attracted significant attention at the Food and Agriculture Organization’s (FAO) Global Exhibition, “From Seeds to Foods”, held in Rome, Italy, from October 8 to 12, 2026.
According to the Sri Lankan Embassy in Rome, the exhibition, held at the historic Circo Massimo as part of the FAO80+1 celebrations, attracted approximately 21,000 visitors from around the world.
Ceylon Tea was a key highlight of Sri Lanka’s participation, with a dedicated stall at the Asia and the Pacific Regional Pavilion offering visitors an opportunity to experience its distinctive flavours and learn about Sri Lanka’s tea heritage.
A special Ceylon Tea tasting session, organized in collaboration with the Sri Lanka Tea Board on October 8, drew considerable interest from visitors.
Sri Lankan street food also took centre stage, with live cooking demonstrations by Chef Praveen Fernando of La Perla Dell’ Asia in Rome, featuring Parippu Vadai and Kottu served alongside Ceylon Tea.
The Kottu demonstration held on October 11 attracted large crowds, with visitors gathering to taste the popular Sri Lankan dish.
Speaking at the event, Sri Lankan Ambassador to Italy Satya Rodrigo described Kottu as a symbol of the country’s diverse culinary traditions.
“Kottu is our street food symphony. You hear the rhythm of the blades before you taste it, and it brings together the flavours of all our communities on one plate,” the Ambassador said.
Meanwhile, Sri Lankan students from the academy of Chanchala Bulathwatta performed a traditional dance titled “Rhythm of Harvest” on October 9, showcasing Sri Lanka’s cultural heritage to an international audience.
The exhibition, organized by the FAO alongside the World Food Forum under the theme “Fostering Innovation for Food Security and Nutrition”, featured six regional pavilions highlighting food traditions, agricultural practices and food security initiatives from across the world.
The Embassy stated that Sri Lanka’s participation was supported by the Sri Lanka Tea Board and the Export Development Board, as part of efforts to promote Sri Lankan products, cuisine and cultural traditions internationally.
articles.summary: Sri Lanka’s world-renowned Ceylon Tea and popular street foods, including Kottu and Parippu Vadai, attracted significant attention at the Food and Agriculture Organization’s (FAO) Global Exhibition, “From Seeds to Foods”, held in Rome, Italy, from October 8 to 12, 2026.

articles.title: Sri Lanka explores oil and gas cooperation with Azerbaijan
articles.text:
Sri Lanka has explored opportunities to strengthen cooperation with Azerbaijan in the energy sector, particularly in oil and gas supply, during discussions between Foreign Minister Vijitha Herath and Azerbaijan President Ilham Aliyev.
The meeting took place in Baku, Azerbaijan, where Minister Herath is leading the Sri Lankan delegation to the 7th Summit of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence Building Measures in Asia (CICA).
In addition to energy cooperation, the discussions focused on strengthening bilateral relations between Sri Lanka and Azerbaijan in trade, investment and tourism.
Minister Herath is attending the 7th CICA Summit, being held in Baku from October 14 to 15, 2026, where he is scheduled to deliver Sri Lanka’s country statement under the theme “Stronger CICA: Connectivity, Digitalisation and Sustainable Growth in Asia.”
During his visit, the Minister is also expected to hold bilateral discussions with representatives of CICA member countries, including Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan and Tajikistan, as well as officials from Azerbaijan and the Secretary-General of CICA.
The visit aims to strengthen Sri Lanka’s diplomatic engagement with Asian countries and explore new economic partnerships, particularly with the growing economies of Central Asia.
CICA is a regional intergovernmental forum that promotes cooperation, peace, security and stability across Asia.

articles.title: Ditwah housing project in Mahiyanganaya nears completion; Minister inspects progress
articles.text:
Minister of Plantations and Community Infrastructure Samantha Vidyarathna has inspected the progress of a housing project for families affected by the Ditwah disaster in Mahiyanganaya, where construction of several houses has reached its final stages.
According to the Ministry of Plantations and Community Infrastructure, the Minister recently visited the project in the Medayaya Grama Niladhari Division to assess the ongoing construction work.
The project, which commenced approximately three months ago, involves the construction of 41 houses, with work progressing rapidly at various stages.
Plans are also underway to provide approximately 30 additional plots of land to other families affected by the disaster.
The project is part of the government’s broader programme to provide permanent housing to 3,748 families in the Badulla District whose homes were completely destroyed or who were residing in high-risk areas.
Under the programme, each beneficiary family will receive Rs. 5 million for house construction, distributed in three instalments of Rs. 2 million, Rs. 1.5 million and Rs. 1.5 million.
The government also plans to provide full freehold deeds for the land allocated for the houses.
Meanwhile, infrastructure development, including access roads, water supply and electricity connections, is being carried out alongside housing construction.
During the visit, Minister Vidyarathna emphasized that the government aims to resettle all disaster-affected families in new houses before the end of this year.

According to the Ministry of Plantations and Community Infrastructure, the Minister recently visited the project in the Medayaya Grama Niladhari Division to assess the ongoing construction work.

articles.title: Sri Lanka turns to alternative countries to address tar shortage
articles.text:
The Road Development Authority (RDA) says Sri Lanka has begun importing tar from alternative countries to address the shortage of supplies required for road development and maintenance, caused by the ongoing conflict in the Middle East.
RDA Director General N. A. Hettiarachchi said Sri Lanka previously relied heavily on high-quality tar manufactured in Iran. However, imports have been disrupted since March due to the ongoing conflict and the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz.
He stated that Sri Lanka requires at least 20,000 metric tonnes of tar per month to carry out road maintenance and development activities across the country.
To address the shortage, the RDA has begun importing limited quantities of tar through alternative routes from Kazakhstan, Bahrain, China, India, Malaysia and Thailand.
However, the Director General noted that despite the availability of alternative markets, transporting tar to Sri Lanka remains a major challenge, with several shipping companies refusing to handle shipments.
He explained that shipping companies are concerned about potential US sanctions and the risk of attacks amid the ongoing conflict.
International insurance providers are also reportedly reluctant to provide coverage for vessels transporting tar due to the prevailing security risks.
These challenges have further complicated efforts to secure a steady supply of tar for Sri Lanka’s road development and maintenance projects.
articles.summary: The Road Development Authority (RDA) says Sri Lanka has begun importing tar from alternative countries to address the shortage of supplies required for road development and maintenance, caused by the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. To address the shortage, the RDA has begun importing limited quantities of tar through alternative routes from Kazakhstan, Bahrain, China, India, Malaysia and Thailand.

articles.title: Bollywood actor told to leave India over election protest
articles.text:
Bollywood actor Imran Khan, nephew of superstar Aamir Khan, has reportedly been ordered to leave India by October 28 after participating in a protest demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
According to Indian media reports, Mumbai Police issued a Leave India Notice to the actor following his participation in a demonstration near August Kranti Maidan in Mumbai on October 10.
Khan, who holds U.S. citizenship and an Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) card, reportedly faces action over allegations that his participation in the political protest violated regulations governing foreign nationals.
The actor was among hundreds of protesters detained by Mumbai Police during the demonstration. He was later released along with his girlfriend, actress Lekha Washington, and his cousin Zayn Marie Khan.
The protest was organised in support of demands for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar amid controversy over India’s electoral processes.
Former Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) lawmaker Kirit Somaiya subsequently called for Khan’s deportation, alleging that his participation in political activities violated conditions applicable to foreign nationals.
The development has also raised questions over the political rights of OCI cardholders, who are permitted to live and work in India but do not enjoy all the rights granted to Indian citizens.
According to The Indian Express, Khan had earlier said he attended the demonstration as a resident of Mumbai and questioned restrictions imposed on people’s freedom of movement and expression.
There has been no confirmation that Khan has left India, while the actor’s response to the latest notice remains unclear.
articles.summary: Bollywood actor Imran Khan, nephew of superstar Aamir Khan, has reportedly been ordered to leave India by October 28 after participating in a protest demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. According to Indian media reports, Mumbai Police issued a Leave India Notice to the actor following his participation in a demonstration near August Kranti Maidan in Mumbai on October 10.

articles.title: Health officials warn Influenza cases on the rise in Sri Lanka
articles.text:
The Epidemiology Unit has reported an increase in influenza cases in Sri Lanka over the past three to four weeks, with around 35% of samples collected last week testing positive for the virus.
Chief Epidemiologist Consultant Dr. Palitha Karunapema said the increase had been identified through the country’s disease surveillance system.
Speaking at a media briefing held at the Health Promotion Bureau, Dr. Karunapema said many of the coughs, colds and fever cases currently being reported are associated with influenza infections.
However, he urged the public not to panic, noting that most patients recover within three to four days with treatment, without developing serious complications.
He warned that certain groups, including pregnant women, young children, the elderly and individuals with underlying health conditions such as diabetes, heart disease and kidney disease, face a higher risk of complications from influenza.
Dr. Karunapema explained that influenza spreads mainly through respiratory droplets released when infected individuals cough or sneeze, as well as through contact.
He advised those experiencing influenza symptoms to remain at home and rest for two to three days to reduce the risk of spreading the infection.
The public was also urged to practise preventive measures, including frequent handwashing with soap and wearing face masks when infected.
Health officials emphasized the importance of taking precautions, particularly among vulnerable groups, while reassuring the public that there is no need for unnecessary fear.
articles.summary: The Epidemiology Unit has reported an increase in influenza cases in Sri Lanka over the past three to four weeks, with around 35% of samples collected last week testing positive for the virus. Speaking at a media briefing held at the Health Promotion Bureau, Dr. Karunapema said many of the coughs, colds and fever cases currently being reported are associated with influenza infections.

articles.title: Israel returns 22 stolen ancient artefacts to Greece
articles.text:
Israel has returned 22 ancient artefacts illegally removed from Greece, marking the first such repatriation between the two countries.
The artefacts were officially handed over to Greek Culture Minister Lina Mendoni during a ceremony at the National Archaeological Museum in Athens on Tuesday (13).
According to Al Jazeera, the collection includes 15 Attic vases, six Corinthian vases and a bronze female statuette, dating from between 700 BC and 320 BC.
The objects were recovered by the Theft Prevention Unit of the Israel Antiquities Authority.
However, officials from both countries did not disclose how the artefacts were discovered in Israel or the circumstances surrounding their illegal removal from Greece.
Speaking at the ceremony, Mendoni described the return as a significant step toward strengthening cooperation between Greece and Israel in protecting cultural heritage.
“Every return of a cultural object to its place of origin has a broader symbolic and moral dimension,” she said.
Israeli Ambassador to Greece Pninat Yanay said the repatriation would help strengthen cooperation between the two countries.
The development comes as Greece and Israel continue to expand their diplomatic, energy and defence relations.
In August, the two countries signed a $3.5 billion defence agreement for the development of a multilayered air defence system in Greece, known as the Achilles Shield.
The agreement is considered one of Israel’s largest defence export deals.
articles.summary: Israel has returned 22 ancient artefacts illegally removed from Greece, marking the first such repatriation between the two countries. However, officials from both countries did not disclose how the artefacts were discovered in Israel or the circumstances surrounding their illegal removal from Greece.

articles.title: Kapila Chandrasena’s phone data at risk of being lost after November 29, Court told
articles.text:
Data linked to the mobile phone of the late former SriLankan Airlines Chief Executive Officer Kapila Chandrasena, who died under mysterious circumstances, could be at risk of being lost after November 29, following a notification from Apple regarding its 90-day data retention period.
The Colombo Crime Division (CCD) informed the Fort Magistrate’s Court on Wednesday (14) that a court order had been forwarded to Apple through the Ministry of Justice under the Mutual Legal Assistance (MLA) process to obtain data from Chandrasena’s mobile phone.
However, Apple had reportedly informed investigators that the relevant data would be retained for only 90 days.
Fort Magistrate Pasan Amarasena, noting that the 90-day period would expire on November 29, questioned whether the data would be lost after the deadline.
Investigating officers informed the court that a further request had been made to Apple, but no response had been received so far.
Expressing dissatisfaction with the progress of the investigation, the Magistrate questioned why the Inspector General of Police (IGP) or the Attorney General (AG) had not been informed about the difficulties in obtaining potentially crucial evidence.
The Magistrate subsequently ordered the CCD to immediately inform the IGP and the Attorney General about the requests made to Apple and take necessary further action.
Meanwhile, the CCD informed the court that the Government Analyst’s reports concerning four types of medication recovered from the location where Chandrasena died had not yet been received, although other reports had been submitted.
The Magistrate observed that Chandrasena had died on May 8 and that the examination of evidence had been completed within a month, yet the relevant Government Analyst’s reports remained pending.
He further remarked that the court alone could not carry out the entire process.
The CCD informed the court that the Government Analyst’s Department had notified investigators on October 13 that another three weeks would be required to provide the outstanding reports relating to the medications.
articles.summary: Data linked to the mobile phone of the late former SriLankan Airlines Chief Executive Officer Kapila Chandrasena, who died under mysterious circumstances, could be at risk of being lost after November 29, following a notification from Apple regarding its 90-day data retention period.

articles.title: Sri Lanka joins global pledge to protect freedom of navigation at sea
articles.text:
Sri Lanka has joined a global pledge to uphold international law at sea and protect freedom of navigation, the European Union (EU) in Sri Lanka announced in a statement on X.
The pledge, announced by EU High Representative and Vice-President Kaja Kallas on October 12, 2026, aims to ensure open waterways while opposing unlawful tolls, fees, discriminatory restrictions and other measures that could obstruct international maritime navigation.
According to the EU, the pledge emphasizes the importance of the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), which establishes the legal framework governing activities in the world’s oceans and seas.
The statement highlights that disruptions to maritime routes, particularly strategically important waterways, have significant consequences for international trade, energy supplies, global supply chains and food security.
It warns that imposing restrictions, discriminatory measures or other obstacles to lawful passage through straits used for international navigation could set a dangerous precedent for global maritime security.
Under the pledge, participating countries have committed to strengthening multilateral cooperation through international and regional institutions, particularly the International Maritime Organization (IMO), to safeguard maritime governance, safety and security.
The countries have also pledged to reject coercive and unilateral actions that undermine international maritime law and oppose unlawful fees, tolls, prior authorization requirements and discriminatory restrictions that interfere with lawful navigation.
The EU further emphasized its support for defensive and non-escalatory multilateral initiatives aimed at preserving freedom of navigation.
The pledge is supported by all EU Member States and 34 countries worldwide, including Sri Lanka, Australia, Canada, Japan, Singapore, the United Kingdom, New Zealand, South Korea, Oman and the Philippines.
articles.summary:
Sri Lanka has joined a global pledge to uphold international law at sea and protect freedom of navigation, the European Union (EU) in Sri Lanka announced in a statement on X.
The pledge, announced by EU High Representative and Vice-President Kaja Kallas on October 12, 2026, aims to ensure open waterways while opposing unlawful tolls, fees, discriminatory restrictions and other measures that could obstruct international maritime navigation.

articles.title: India busts USD 3.15 million Pakistani goods smuggling racket via Colombo Port
articles.text:
India’s Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) has uncovered an alleged smuggling operation involving Pakistani-origin goods transported through Sri Lanka to India using fraudulent trade documents, with four individuals arrested in connection with the racket.
According to India’s Ministry of Finance, the operation involved more than 7.3 million kilograms of Pakistani-origin rock salt valued at over USD 3.15 million (INR 30 crore).
Investigations revealed that nine importers had brought 295 containers of the goods into India through the Mundra and Kandla ports since March 2026, despite restrictions on imports of Pakistani-origin goods.
The shipments were allegedly routed through Colombo Port by a UAE-based company, with fabricated trade documents used to conceal their Pakistani origin.
Indian authorities conducted a special operation between September 26 and October 11, identifying the shipments and seizing five containers carrying approximately 140 metric tonnes of rock salt.
The investigation also revealed that customs declarations submitted in Sri Lanka had correctly identified Pakistan as the country of origin and India as the final destination.
However, fraudulent certificates were allegedly used during the Indian import process to misrepresent the origin of the goods and bypass import restrictions.
Authorities said the network involved businesses owned by Pakistani, UAE, Sri Lankan and Indian nationals.
Four individuals have been arrested, while further investigations are underway to identify others involved in the alleged smuggling operation.
articles.summary: India’s Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) has uncovered an alleged smuggling operation involving Pakistani-origin goods transported through Sri Lanka to India using fraudulent trade documents, with four individuals arrested in connection with the racket. According to India’s Ministry of Finance, the operation involved more than 7.3 million kilograms of Pakistani-origin rock salt valued at over USD 3.15 million (INR 30 crore).

articles.title: Monk accused of spreading false claims about attack on supporter of protest march
articles.text:
Sri Lanka Police have rejected claims that a man was attacked for supporting a protest march from Kandy to Colombo demanding the release of imprisoned Buddhist monk Ven. Galagoda Aththe Gnanasara Thera.
In a statement, police said the incident occurred on Oct. 14 in the Weeragula police area and was the result of a traffic-related dispute rather than an attack connected to the protest march.
The clarification follows a video circulating on social media in which Ven. Thiththagalle Anandasiri Thera claimed that a man who had assisted the march was assaulted by a group of individuals using a helmet.
However, police said preliminary investigations revealed that the injured man was not associated with the protest march and had been travelling in a lorry for personal reasons when the incident occurred.
According to a statement obtained from the injured man, an argument broke out between him and a motorcyclist during traffic congestion near the Veediyawatta Devalaya. The disagreement subsequently escalated into a physical confrontation involving a helmet.
The injured man was admitted to Wathupitiwala Hospital for treatment, while the motorcyclist involved in the dispute was also admitted to Gampaha Hospital.
Police said their investigations indicated that Ven. Anandasiri Thera had recorded a video showing the injured man’s wounds while presenting him as a supporter of the protest march who had been attacked.
However, police maintained that the incident was unrelated to the march and accused the monk of spreading false information through social media.
Weeragula Police are expected to report the matter to court.
Police also warned that legal action would be considered against individuals spreading false or unverified information that could create public unrest.
The public has been urged to exercise caution when sharing videos and claims circulating on social media.
Further investigations are underway.
articles.summary: Sri Lanka Police have rejected claims that a man was attacked for supporting a protest march from Kandy to Colombo demanding the release of imprisoned Buddhist monk Ven. articles.title: Expert Committee Report on Election Law reviews submitted to Parliamentary Select Committee
articles.text:
The expert committee report detailing public views and proposals for the review of election laws has been officially submitted to the Parliamentary Select Committee tasked with examining laws dealing with elections, excluding those governing provincial council elections.
The report was handed over to the Chairman of the Select Committee Minister of Public Administration, Provincial Councils and Local Government, Prof. Chandana Abayarathna by the expert committee appointed to review public submissions.
The expert committee was originally formed to conduct an in-depth review of 31 proposals submitted by members of the public, institutions and organizations, alongside reports from previous parliamentary select committees appointed to examine election related matters.
Commenting on the process, Minister Abayarathna noted that separate reports had been prepared and submitted regarding the various issues and themes raised by organizations and institutions.
He further stated that several registered political parties have also submitted their views and proposals. The Parliamentary Select Committee intends to review all submissions made by the public, institutions, organizations and political parties and present an interim report to Parliament within two months. He added that citizens and members of the public will still be given a further opportunity to submit amendments and new proposals even after the interim report is submitted.
Meanwhile, the committee decided to extend by an additional two weeks the deadline granted to registered political parties to submit their views and proposals on the review of these election related laws.

articles.title: Reconstruction of Ditwah damaged Badulu Oya Irrigation Scheme reaches final stage
articles.text:
Permanent restoration work on the Badulu Oya Irrigation Scheme, which was severely damaged by the Ditwah disaster, has reached its final stage following four months of intensive rehabilitation efforts.
The permanent reconstruction initiative was officially launched on June 5 under the patronage of Plantation and Community Infrastructure Minister Samantha Vidyaratne.
Following the initial disaster, authorities implemented temporary water distribution measures using sandbags in January, before commencing permanent repairs in June. Under the project, a 2km section of the main canal has been completely repaired and concrete lined.
A team led by Deputy Minister of Youth Affairs Dinindu Saman Hennayake recently conducted a field visit to inspect the project’s progress.
Despite operating with a limited workforce, staff and engineers from the Irrigation Department managed to complete the large-scale reconstruction within four months.
The fully restored scheme feeds over 1,775 acres of farmland, offering a permanent solution to the water scarcity previously faced by local farmers.

St. Joseph’s College, Colombo 10, is marking a rare milestone in its educational history as Mrs Nimala Perera celebrates 50 years of service to the College on 14 October 2026 , recognising a career that has influenced generations of Josephians.
Currently serving as Deputy Principal – Administration , Mrs Perera has spent five decades as an educator and administrator at St. Joseph’s, becoming a familiar and respected presence to generations of students, parents, teachers and old boys. Recent accounts of the College’s history also identify her as one of its longest-serving educators and as a member of the present administration.
Fifty years at a single school represents a remarkable period of continuity. During that time, education has undergone major changes, from teaching methods and curricula to technology and the expectations placed on both students and educators. Through those changes, Mrs Perera’s contribution has remained closely associated with discipline, academic standards, student development and the values of St. Joseph’s College .
The milestone is particularly significant in the context of the College’s own long history. St. Joseph’s was officially opened on 2 March 1896 and has developed over more than a century into one of Sri Lanka’s prominent Catholic educational institutions. Its stated mission places emphasis not only on educational excellence, but also on spiritual and human values and preparing students with the knowledge, skills and character to serve society.
For many Josephians, Mrs Perera’s contribution has extended well beyond the classroom. Her career has encompassed teaching, administration, student guidance and participation in the wider life of the College.
Her association with student leadership has also spanned decades. The official profile of the Interact Club of St. Joseph’s College records Mrs Perera as its first Staff Adviser following the club’s inauguration in 1980 and notes her continued involvement more than four decades later reflecting a longstanding commitment to encouraging service, leadership and responsibility among students.
Her presence has also been documented at numerous College initiatives over the years. In 2016, for example, she was identified as Upper School Principal during a student-focused initiative at St. Joseph’s, while later accounts record her progression to senior administrative leadership.
What makes the Golden Jubilee especially meaningful is the number of generations touched by her service. Former students paying tribute to Mrs Perera describe an educator who has taught not only individual boys, but in some cases members of the same families across different generations.
Old Josephian Guruji Ravindhiran Maruthai , in a tribute marking the anniversary, described Mrs Perera as more than part of the College’s history, saying: “You are not just a part of our College’s history; you are the heart.”
His tribute reflects the personal connection many former students associate with teachers whose influence continues long after school life has ended.
For educators, the impact of a career is rarely measured only through examination results. It is also found in the confidence built in students, the standards passed from one generation to another, the discipline instilled during difficult moments and the values former pupils continue to carry into adulthood.
Mrs Perera’s 50 year journey represents that broader contribution.
As St. Joseph’s College itself continues to evolve, her Golden Jubilee provides an opportunity to recognise the role played by educators who provide stability across generations while adapting to a changing educational landscape.
It is also a reminder of the enduring importance of teachers in shaping not only successful students, but responsible citizens and future leaders.
For the Josephian community, 14 October 2026 marks more than a service anniversary . It celebrates five decades of teaching, leadership, mentorship and commitment to an institution whose motto, “In Scientia et Virtute” – “In Knowledge and in Virtue” , has guided generations of students.
As Mrs Nimala Perera marks her Golden Jubilee at St. Joseph’s College, her legacy can perhaps be measured most meaningfully not simply in years, but in the thousands of Josephians who passed through the College during those five decades carrying with them lessons, values and memories shaped in part by an educator who remained a constant presence through a changing world.
– G. Ravindhiran and Senal Warnakula

articles.title: Taxpayers reminded to submit income tax returns by November 30
articles.text:
The Inland Revenue Department (IRD) has reminded taxpayers that the deadline for submitting income tax returns for the Year of Assessment 2025/2026 is November 30, 2026.
Issuing a notice to taxpayers, the department urged those required to file income tax returns to ensure their submissions are completed by the specified deadline.
Taxpayers seeking further information or clarification regarding the submission of income tax returns can contact the Inland Revenue Department through its hotline, 1944.
Additional information is also available on the department’s official website, www.ird.gov.lk .

articles.title: Sri Lanka joins first BIMSTEC Home Ministers’ Meeting in India
articles.text:
Sri Lanka’s Minister of Public Security, Ananda Wijepala, participated in the first BIMSTEC Home Ministers’ Meeting held in New Delhi, India, on Wednesday (Oct. 14).
The meeting was hosted by India under the chairmanship of Union Home Minister Amit Shah, bringing together ministers from member countries of the Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation (BIMSTEC).
The discussions focused on strengthening regional cooperation to address evolving security threats and promoting a safer, more secure and resilient Bay of Bengal region.
The initiative reflects a shared commitment among BIMSTEC member states to enhance cooperation in addressing regional security challenges.
Minister Wijepala expressed appreciation to Indian Home Minister Amit Shah and the Government of India for hosting the inaugural meeting and bringing regional partners together to advance common security objectives.
BIMSTEC comprises seven member countries: Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Thailand.
