articles.title: PM hails Sri Lanka’s $9 Bn export performance in first half of 2026
articles.text:
Sri Lanka’s total exports surpassed USD 9 billion during the first half of 2026, Prime Minister Harini Amarasuriya has stated, highlighting positive signs in the country’s economic performance.
The Prime Minister made the remarks in connection with the 26th Sri Lanka Economic and Investment Summit (SLEIS) 2026, held on October 12 and 13.
According to the Prime Minister’s Media Division, PM Amarasuriya participated in the summit on Tuesday (13), addressing a session titled “Nation Building in the Digital Age.”
During her address, the Prime Minister outlined the government’s ambition to expand Sri Lanka’s digital economy to USD 15 billion by 2030, increase digital exports to USD 5 billion and develop a workforce of 200,000 digital professionals.
She said the government was committed to transforming Sri Lanka from a consumer of technology into a creator of innovation.
The Prime Minister further revealed that approximately Rs. 30 billion had been committed towards foundational digital transformation initiatives through the Ministry of Digital Economy.
Highlighting progress in digital public services, she said the GovPay platform had processed over Rs. 6 billion in payments, with more than 300 organisations connected to the system.
PM Amarasuriya also highlighted the potential of digital technologies to improve healthcare, agriculture, energy and transport services, while stressing the importance of ensuring equal access to digital opportunities.
Meanwhile, she revealed that a five-year plan had been developed in collaboration with the Ministry of Digital Economy to improve digital readiness across Sri Lanka’s education system.
The Prime Minister also called for stronger cooperation between the government, private sector and educational institutions to expand vocational training and prepare the workforce for emerging employment opportunities.
She emphasised that the integration of artificial intelligence into education must be carefully managed to avoid widening existing inequalities and negatively affecting students’ critical thinking and cognitive development.
The summit brought together policymakers, investors, business leaders and other stakeholders to discuss Sri Lanka’s economic prospects and investment opportunities.
articles.summary: Sri Lanka’s total exports surpassed USD 9 billion during the first half of 2026, Prime Minister Harini Amarasuriya has stated, highlighting positive signs in the country’s economic performance. During her address, the Prime Minister outlined the government’s ambition to expand Sri Lanka’s digital economy to USD 15 billion by 2030, increase digital exports to USD 5 billion and develop a workforce of 200,000 digital professionals.

articles.title: New prison rules proposed to allow Buddhist monks to wear robes outside prison
articles.text:
Justice and National Integration Minister Harshana Nanayakkara has announced proposed amendments to prison regulations that would allow imprisoned Buddhist monks to wear their robes when leaving prison for court appearances or other purposes.
The proposals follow discussions between President Anura Kumara Dissanayake and representatives of the three Buddhist Nikayas over concerns surrounding the removal of Ven. Galagoda Aththe Gnanasara Thera’s robes following his imprisonment.
Speaking at the Justice Ministry today (14), Minister Nanayakkara said a committee appointed by the President had submitted its interim report recommending amendments to existing prison standing orders.
Under the proposed amendments, Buddhist monks serving prison sentences would be permitted to wear their robes when leaving prison unless the relevant Buddhist chapter or Nikaya directs otherwise.
The committee has also recommended amending Standing Order 356 to introduce a procedure requiring prison authorities to notify the Department of Buddhist Affairs regarding the removal of a monk’s robes upon imprisonment.
The Commissioner of Prisons would be given 10 days to take the necessary action in consultation with the department.
The minister said similar provisions would apply, with appropriate modifications, to clergy of other faiths.
He said the interim report had already been forwarded to the acting Commissioner General of Prisons, with instructions to amend the relevant standing orders in accordance with the committee’s recommendations.
The proposed changes follow concerns raised by senior Buddhist monks over the treatment of imprisoned clergy.
The minister said the President had promised to address the issue within two weeks during discussions with Buddhist religious leaders.
The amendments have been recommended but have not yet been confirmed as implemented.
articles.summary: Justice and National Integration Minister Harshana Nanayakkara has announced proposed amendments to prison regulations that would allow imprisoned Buddhist monks to wear their robes when leaving prison for court appearances or other purposes. Under the proposed amendments, Buddhist monks serving prison sentences would be permitted to wear their robes when leaving prison unless the relevant Buddhist chapter or Nikaya directs otherwise.

articles.title: Two ministry cabs broke down, had to use friend’s vehicle: Minister Lal Kantha
articles.text:
Minister K.D. Lal Kantha has revealed that two double cabs assigned to him by his ministry broke down during official travel, forcing him to use a private vehicle belonging to a close friend to carry out his duties.
Addressing a public event, the Minister said he had been using two double cabs obtained from his ministry, but recently experienced mechanical problems with both vehicles.
He explained that one of the vehicles broke down midway through a journey, prompting him to arrange for the second cab. However, the replacement vehicle also broke down after travelling a short distance.
As a result, he said he was compelled to use a vehicle belonging to a close friend to continue his official duties.
Minister Lal Kantha said the government was facing a shortage of suitable vehicles and other facilities, stressing the need to provide new vehicles for official use.
He also highlighted the deteriorating condition of several government-owned buildings, noting that some official residences and properties were in poor condition, with damaged roofs, broken washrooms and a lack of maintenance.
The Minister said that although a new government had assumed office, it had inherited several shortcomings in state facilities and infrastructure. He further claimed that ministers had not obtained additional privileges or benefits since assuming office.
Meanwhile, commenting on the global situation, Minister Lal Kantha claimed that the government had taken measures to minimise the impact of international conflicts on Sri Lanka.
He said the government had ensured the continued functioning of essential services despite global challenges and claimed that Sri Lanka was providing fuel at one of the lowest prices.

articles.title: Namal writes to President, seeks second-chance loan scheme in 2027 Budget
articles.text:
Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna (SLPP) MP Namal Rajapaksa has called on President and Finance Minister Anura Kumara Dissanayake to introduce a second-chance business loan scheme in the 2027 Budget to help entrepreneurs who have fully repaid their debts regain access to credit.
In a letter to the President, Rajapaksa said individuals who had experienced repayment difficulties in the past but subsequently settled their loans in full continued to face significant obstacles in obtaining fresh credit due to their records with the Credit Information Bureau (CRIB).
He said historical information on repaid loans remained in CRIB records for up to five years, potentially affecting borrowers’ ability to secure new loans, although CRIB did not blacklist individuals.
Citing Malaysia’s Central Credit Reference Information System (CCRIS) as an example, Rajapaksa said the system updated loan statuses following full repayment and primarily reflected repayment histories covering the preceding 12 months.
He proposed five measures for inclusion in the 2027 Budget, including updating CRIB records within five working days of full loan repayment and clearly marking settled loans as “Fully Settled/Closed”.
He also called for guidelines requiring banks to assess loan applications based not only on past credit difficulties but also on applicants’ current income and repayment capacity.
Furthermore, he proposed reviewing the period for which historical credit information was retained in Sri Lanka, taking international practices into consideration.
Rajapaksa also called for a “Second-Chance Business Loan Scheme” to help micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) that had settled all their debt obligations restart their businesses.
A person who had previously struggled to repay a loan but had subsequently settled the debt in full should be given another opportunity to contribute to the economy, he said, adding that such measures would benefit both entrepreneurs and the country’s economic growth.
He urged the Government to introduce a prompt and lasting solution to the issue through the 2027 Budget.
articles.summary: Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna (SLPP) MP Namal Rajapaksa has called on President and Finance Minister Anura Kumara Dissanayake to introduce a second-chance business loan scheme in the 2027 Budget to help entrepreneurs who have fully repaid their debts regain access to credit.
